raw_response:
I have farmed here in Quzhou for 15 years, so I do not change too much just for the sake of changing. On 225 mu, I need stable grain first, then cash crops for margin. Wheat-maize on 120 mu is still my backbone because it is reliable and fits our land and irrigation well. Chili and stevia bring better cash if the market is decent, but they cost more and need more hands, so I keep them on part of the farm instead of pushing everything into one crop. I finished middle school, so I do look at rate and timing, but I still decide mainly from what worked on my fields and what the stronger growers nearby are doing.

For wheat, I will not cut fertilizer too hard because if wheat goes yellow in spring, yield drops fast and it is hard to recover. For maize, the key is fast turnaround after wheat harvest, so I will use rotary tillage and machine sowing and get it in within a few days. Chili needs more water, potassium, and spraying, so I keep it to 60 mu because it ties up cash and labor. Stevia is a decent cash crop for me, but I manage it more carefully and do not overfeed nitrogen, otherwise the stand grows too soft and quality can suffer. Since I have a well, I will irrigate when the crop stage matters, but I still watch pumping cost, so I will not water unless the soil is really short.
